ana: Heads-up, the int4 bring-up on staging shows weird metric divergence vs our float baseline :thinking_face:
ana: Float32 NDCG@5=0.362, int4 NDCG@5=0.333 (big), but MRR@1 bumped 0.178 -> 0.185
ana: That smells like top-1 swaps improving short queries while tail ordering collapses
tony: Did we run the same candidate pool and ranking harness? Sometimes the harness dedup step reorders candidates
ana: Yes same cands.jsonl and seed. Command I used:
ana: ```
./eval_reranker --model rerank-v3-int4 --candidates /mnt/eval/cands_2026.jsonl --metrics ndcg@5,mrr@1 --seed 2026 --no-dedupe
```
rui: Our CI eval uses --dedupe by default; production scoring does not. Could be the difference point
ana: Good catch. When I re-ran with --dedupe the NDCG gap shrank to 0.018 (0.362 -> 0.344)
tony: So dedupe is masking some tie-breaking noise in int4. But we should still understand why int4 prefers shorter snippet forms for top-1
katya: Could tokenizer normalization be different between quant conversion step and eval runtime? I remember a case with punctuation stripping causing tie flips
ana: I validated tokenizer version: both use tokenizerv2@1.4 but conversion script used --do_lower True while runtime had casefold disabled. I'll re-run with explicit casefold to match
ana: Quick per-length bucket snapshot (sample 1k queries):
- short (<=6 tokens): float NDCG@5 0.285, int4 0.292
- mid (7-20 tokens): float 0.374, int4 0.350
- long (>20 tokens): float 0.410, int4 0.358
ana: So long anchors take the biggest hit
tony: That aligns with kvpack alignment/quant scale failure on long contexts. Did you check softmax/logit scaling in qconfig?
ana: Not yet. I also noticed the eval harness truncates passages at 512 tokens, but prod scoring keeps full doc. That could change kv offsets
rui: Two things to do: (1) reproduce on single node float vs int4 back-to-back (to rule out infra jitter), (2) produce per-query delta file so we can bootstrap p-values and find clusters of failure
ana: I'll trigger a parity job on r-infer-07 now and attach per-query delta JSONL to /mnt/eval/parity_int4_run.jsonl
ci-bot: nightly-evals queued (job=nb-18700). Expect ~18m for 1k queries. Report will include per-query swapped ranks and histograms
katya: Also add an ablation run: int4 but with full-precision softmax (if runtime supports) and int4 with kvpack disabled
tony: Good idea. If softmax precision helps, it's a numerical stability issue at the output layer not attention internals
ana: Running additional ablations: int4+fp-softmax, int4+no-kvpack, int8 baseline. Will post numbers when done
ana: Interim results (200q quick-run):
- float32 NDCG@5 0.3619 MRR@1 0.1784
- int4 NDCG@5 0.3327 MRR@1 0.1851
- int4+fp-softmax NDCG@5 0.3478 MRR@1 0.1830
- int4+no-kvpack NDCG@5 0.3512 MRR@1 0.1815
- int8 NDCG@5 0.3589 MRR@1 0.1792
ana: fp-softmax and disabling kvpack both recover ~half the gap. int8 is closest to float as expected
katya: That suggests output numerical precision plus kv alignment both contribute. We should add a small regression test into the eval-harness to catch this specific pattern (long anchors + priming)
tony: Agreed. Suggest the test include a curated set of 500 long-anchor queries and require ndcg@5 drop < 0.02 vs float. Fail the presubmit for model-conversion PRs if violated
ana: I'll author the test and upload the corpus to /mnt/eval/int4_triage_longanchors.jsonl
rui: For rollout plan: canary int4 only in routes with short-anchor traffic (low risk) until we disable the two risky features (prefix kvpack and fp-softmax fallback) or fix kernel quantization
katya: Ops note: disabling kvpack hurts latency by ~10-15% on p50 for rerank pipelines. We need to balance cost/latency vs quality
ana: Follow-ups assigned: ana (per-query deltas + test corpus), tony (kernel qconfig trace for softmax), rui (parity runs and canary plan), katya (impact analysis on latency/cost)
ana: Tagging @here since this affects the int4 rollout window :warning:
rui: acknowledged :+1:
